isThe855CheckVerifierCircular.answer: Yes, in part. 136 of its 855 checks read the record's own claim back as its own proof, and one further class of check is seeded by the record rather than by the source.

circularChecks.what: asserts record.createsApproval === false, opensNoRoute === true and four siblings — the record's own self-description, proved by itself
statuses.length <= 1 is computed over family.routes[].ratification.status, the record's own copy of the status

vocabulary.paymentAuthority === 'closed' reads record.treatmentVocabulary, which the same lane wrote; it never checks that guidance_status/referral/unsupported are actually in NO_PARTICIPANT_FILING_OUTCOMES in src/lib/legal-authority/types.ts

the four checkout claims — packetCheckout, packetCreditConsumption, partnerCreditConsumption, renderJobAllowed — are asserted against the record's own fields. renderJobAllowed is the check that matters, and it is exactly the claim this lane measured false on 9 routes
retiredPacket.disposition and retiredPacket.bytesMoved are the record's own assertions read back; the real byte proof is the hashing at 308-321
the open-item list is compared against record.families[].packetStillResolvesOnThisRoute — record against record; its only tie to reality is the check at 369, which skips null-routeKey routes

seededRatherThanDerived: lines 107-111: STATUS_TO_TREATMENT is a retyped copy of the record's own howTheTreatmentIsDecided.statusToTreatment. The registry's statusVocabulary contains no treatment words, so the mapping is not derivable from the source; the verifier never even checks that its copy agrees with the record's. The header claim that the treatment word is 'recomputed from the ratified status without reading the record's answer' overstates what lines 129-135 do.

line 139: `if (!route.ratification.routeKey) continue;` means a route the record writes as routeKey null is never checked against the registry at all. A record that wrote null over a route that DOES have a registry row would be handed the question-derived treatment and pass. This lane confirmed independently that CT, NV and SD genuinely have no registry row, so the gap is not exploited — but it is open.
line 331: `if (!route.routeKey) continue;` excludes both Connecticut routes from every runtime measurement, so 2 of the 19 routes are never resolved at all.
whatItDoesMeasureHonestly: 83 of 83 declared sha256 values, recomputed here and all matching
the participant-facing quotes, against the legal-design track registry and the committed build findings
sellable, creditConsumable and availability through a real resolvePacketRoute call on 17 of 19 routes
the seven contract flips, through legalRouteContract and routePaymentAuthority
the canonical PDFs, field maps and instruction files, by hash
whatItCannotCatch: a render job specification that still builds — it never calls buildRenderJobSpec
a deleted or rewritten boundary PDF — 23 of them carry no hash
a route the record writes as routeKey null
a false preservation sentence inside a route contract's notes (the OR duplicate)

families.verdictScope: The treatment WORD is correctly read from its controlling record and the route is genuinely not sellable and not credit-consumable. What is unsupported is the record's runtimeExpression and its checkout.renderJobAllowed=false: no legal-authority route contract exists for these routes, so routePaymentAuthority — the derivation the record names — is never called on them, and buildRenderJobSpec still returns a render job specification with rendererKind packet_document_v1.
